findings.summary:
The five tabs are one `TabView(selection:)` with five `NavigationStack` roots, tagged `.chat/.documents/.visualizations/.database/.settings` (/Users/gunnarhostetler/Documents/GitHub/OpenIntelligence/OpenIntelligence/App/ContentView.swift:254-304). Three things in this dimension are clean and I want to say so rather than pad: (a) no `.id()` is applied to any container anywhere in the app — the only `.id()` calls are per-row identity inside scroll content (MessageListV2.swift:77-119, ThinkingStreamView.swift:152, IngestionQueueOverlay.swift:75), so nothing forces a tab teardown; (b) no view model is built in a `View.init` — every long-lived object is a `@StateObject` on ContentView (ContentView.swift:14-21) or a shared singleton, and the five tab roots have trivial or absent inits (ChatScreen.swift:194, DocumentLibraryView.swift:84), so declaring all five in one ViewBuilder costs nothing; (c) `@State` genuinely survives tab switches, so selections, sheet flags and expanded sections come back intact.

The defects are all one shape, and it is the opposite of the one I expected: state survives, but appearance callbacks throw it away. Every tab root restarts its `.task`/`onAppear` when the user returns, and four of the five then either recompute from zero while showing a spinner over data that is still in memory, or actively destroy user work. The worst is Chat: returning to the tab mid-answer runs the container-change task from the top, which cancels the streaming query and discards the partial text — the "Stop" button preserves the partial answer, this path does not. Second worst is that the transcript force-scrolls to the bottom on every return, so you cannot leave the tab while reading an older answer. Atlas, its 3D scene, and the Database overview each replace populated content with a loading state on return; the visualization engine even maintains a `profileCache` that is written and never read (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:304, 381).

Separately, navigation is not addressable: no `NavigationStack` in the app takes a `path` binding (only the Glossary does, GlossaryViews.swift:179), so deep links and Spotlight can select a tab but cannot reach its root, re-tapping the active tab does nothing, and there is no `@SceneStorage` anywhere — tab selection and the composer draft do not survive a relaunch.

Everything below is read off source. The premise that SwiftUI restarts `.task` and fires `onAppear`/`onDisappear` on a `TabView` tab change needs a device confirmation, though the repo already contains strong circumstantial evidence for it: ChatScreen keeps an `isAppeared` flag set in `onAppear`/`onDisappear` (ChatScreen.swift:885, 888) specifically to defer suggested-question refreshes while the Chat tab is not showing, which only makes sense if the author observed those callbacks firing on tab switches.

One out-of-dimension note in passing, since the brief asked to treat the chip/scroll-gesture conflict as a pattern: SourceChipsView.swift:126 attaches `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0, pressing:)` to a `Button` that already has `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, inside a horizontal `ScrollView` (line 34). It is the same recognizer-versus-pan shape as the library chips, and the press state it drives is already available from the button style. Whoever owns the gesture dimension should look at it.

issues.what: Returning to the Chat tab while an answer is streaming cancels the query and discards the partial text. The `.task(id: activeContainerId)` body runs on every appearance, not only when the container id changes, and its first four statements cancel the in-flight query unconditionally — before the `isSameChatContainer` guard that scopes the rest of the body.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You ask a question, glance at Documents to check a filename, come back, and the answer is gone with no explanation — no partial text, no error, just an idle composer. It teaches you that you are not allowed to leave the Chat tab, which is the exact opposite of seamless tab switching. `stopGeneration()` (line 1818) keeps the partial answer as a message; this path calls `resetStreamingState()` and keeps nothing.
issues.fix: Track the container the task last reset for in a `@State var lastCancelledContainerId: UUID?` and wrap lines 601-615 in `if lastCancelledContainerId != activeId { ... }`, or simply move the cancel block inside the existing `if !isSameChatContainer` branch that already computes exactly this condition at line 623. Nothing else in the body needs to change.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The cross-container bleed protection the comment at line 604 describes is fully kept — it fires on a real container change, which is the only case the comment names. The `isSameChatContainer`/`isSameDocsContainer` guards at lines 623-624 already prove the author's intent was per-container, not per-appearance: history reload, suggested-question invalidation and count recalculation are all already gated that way, and only the cancellation block was left ungated. Manual stop (line 1818) and scene-phase cancellation (line 590) are untouched.

issues.what: The chat transcript force-scrolls to the bottom on every appearance. `onAppear` calls `scrollToBottom(animated: false)` with no guard, overriding the `isPinnedToBottom` state the view already maintains for exactly this purpose.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You scroll up to re-read an earlier answer, switch to Documents to check something against it, come back — and you are slammed to the newest message, with a visible 0.12s animated jump because `animated: false` still wraps the call in `withAnimation` (line 164). Finding your place again is manual work the app just undid for you.
issues.fix: Add `@State private var hasPerformedInitialScroll = false` and in `onAppear` scroll only when `!hasPerformedInitialScroll || isPinnedToBottom`, setting the flag afterwards. Keep `scrollProxy = proxy` unconditional.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The first-open jump to the newest message is kept (the flag is false on first appearance). All streaming auto-follow is untouched — the three `onChange` handlers at lines 131, 135 and 145 already gate on `isPinnedToBottom` and do the real scroll-following work. `isPinnedToBottom` is already computed from the bottom-anchor preference at line 152, so the information needed for the guard exists and is currently just ignored.

issues.what: The Atlas tab replaces its entire populated body with a loading card every time it appears. Two `.task` modifiers both call `refreshAnalysis()` on appearance (the bare one at 205 and the id-keyed one at 208), `analyze()` sets the published `isAnalyzing = true` before doing any work (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:359), and the body renders `analyzeLoadingCard` whenever that flag is true (line 123) even though `engine.currentProfile` still holds a valid, complete profile.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Atlas is the tab you flick to in order to glance at something. Instead of the insights and stats you left, you get a spinner card, the page collapses to a fraction of its height so your scroll position is clamped to the top, and then everything reflows back in. The data never left memory — the app just refuses to show it while it re-derives the same result.
issues.fix: Three edits, all local: delete the bare `.task` at 205 (the `.task(id:)` at 208 already runs on appearance and on id change, so coverage is identical and the duplicate analysis disappears); in `LibraryVisualizationEngine.analyze`, serve `profileCache[containerId]` into `currentProfile` synchronously when present before starting the rebuild; and change the gate at line 123 to `if engine.isAnalyzing, engine.currentProfile == nil`.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every refresh still happens on the same triggers — appearance, container change, and pull-to-refresh (line 210) — because the id-keyed task fires on both of the first two. Nothing is cached longer than it is now: `profileCache` is already populated on every successful analysis at LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:381 and already invalidated per container at line 341 and wholesale at 331 (ContentView.swift:395 calls the per-container invalidation on library removal), so reading it is completing a mechanism that is already fully wired and currently dead. The loading card still shows on genuine first load, when `currentProfile` is nil.

issues.what: The compact 3D atlas scene discards its rendered point cloud on every appearance. Two `.task(id:)` modifiers both fire on appear (2897, 2900), each calls `loadAndProject()`, and its first statement sets `isLoading = true` (line 3029), which swaps the SceneKit view for a spinner while up to 50,000 points are re-fetched from FTS5 and re-projected — twice, concurrently.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The 3D atlas is the one thing in the app you orient yourself in — you rotate it to a view you like. Coming back to the tab throws away both the render and your camera position, and you watch it rebuild from a spinner. The `points`, `colors` and `annotations` arrays are still sitting in `@State` the whole time.
issues.fix: Collapse the two modifiers into one `.task(id: AtlasReloadKey(container: containerService.activeContainerId, projection: projectionMethod))` over a small `Equatable` struct, and in `loadAndProject()` set `isLoading = true` only when `points.isEmpty`, assigning the new arrays when the projection finishes.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Both reload triggers are kept verbatim: a composite Equatable key changes when either the container or the projection method changes, which is precisely the union of what the two separate ids covered. The empty-library path at line 3046 still clears the arrays and drops the spinner. The five `onChange` handlers at 2903-2907 that reload the scene for point scale, rotation, depth cue, labels and background are untouched.

issues.what: The Database tab shows "Loading database statistics..." on every return. `.task { await loadAllData() }` restarts on appearance and `loadAllData` sets `isLoading = true` at line 215 before querying, while the overview section gates its whole body on that flag at line 492 — even though `stats` and `documentStats` are still populated from the previous visit.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Database is a reference tab you bounce in and out of while working. Every bounce costs a spinner and a scroll reset on the default section, for numbers that were on screen ten seconds ago and are still in memory. The 10-second watchdog at line 218 tells you the author already knows this load can be slow — which is exactly why the previous result should stay visible during it.
issues.fix: Set `isLoading = true` at line 215 only when `stats == nil`, and change the gate at line 492 to `if isLoading, stats == nil`. Optionally add a small inline refreshing indicator in `headerSection` so the refresh is still legible.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every phase still runs on every appearance — Phase 1 metadata, Phase 2 diagnostics and vocabulary in the detached task, Phase 3 content-table backfill. The watchdog at line 218 keeps working because it reads the same flag. `.refreshable` (line 196) and the scope-change reload (line 187) are untouched. No query is skipped or cached; only the decision to blank the screen while they run changes.

issues.what: The ingestion queue overlay exists as two independent instances — one in Chat (ChatScreen.swift:520) and one in Documents (DocumentLibraryView.swift:1327) — each holding its own `@State isMinimized` and `@State isDismissed`. Dismissing or minimizing it on one tab has no effect on the other.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You dismiss the ingestion panel to get it out of the way, switch tabs, and it is back at full size — so the dismissal reads as broken rather than tab-scoped. Worse in the other direction: you minimise it on Documents to watch progress compactly, go to Chat, and it expands over the composer again. Dismissal is a statement about the panel, not about the tab you happened to be on.
issues.fix: Introduce a small `@MainActor final class IngestionOverlayPresentation: ObservableObject` holding `isMinimized`/`isDismissed`, own it as a `@StateObject` in ContentView alongside the other stores, inject it with `.environmentObject`, and have `IngestionQueueOverlay` read it instead of its two local `@State` properties.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every control, item row, cancel/continue/discard callback and console view stays exactly as it is — only where the two booleans live changes. The auto-reset on an emptied queue (line 475) and the deep-link un-dismiss handler (line 481) keep working unchanged against the shared object, and the deep link actually improves: it currently un-dismisses both copies blindly, and would instead un-dismiss the one panel that exists.

issues.what: No tab's `NavigationStack` takes a `path` binding, so nothing can programmatically return a tab to its root. `handleOpenURL` and the Spotlight handler set `selectedTab` only; if the target tab has a pushed detail view, the user lands on that detail instead of the destination the link named.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Tap a Spotlight result for a document while the Documents tab happens to be showing a different document's details, and you arrive at the wrong document with the app insisting it navigated. Same for the `openintelligence://documents/ingestion` deep link, which posts its overlay notification (line 419) to a screen you cannot see. It also means re-tapping the already-selected tab does nothing, breaking the pop-to-root gesture every iOS user has in their hands.
issues.fix: Add `@State private var documentsPath = NavigationPath()` (and equivalents for the other tabs that push), bind them into the `NavigationStack(path:)` initialisers at 255/263/275/285/295, clear the relevant path in `handleOpenURL` (line 416) and in the Spotlight handler (line 108) before assigning `selectedTab`, and add a `selectedTab` binding wrapper whose setter clears the path when the new value equals the old.
issues.functionalityPreserved: `NavigationStack` tracks `NavigationLink(destination:)` pushes in its bound path as well as value-based links, so the existing document-row link (DocumentLibraryView.swift:204), the Settings links (SettingsView.swift:322) and the diagnostics hub links all keep working with no call-site change. This adds reachability; it removes no destination and no way of getting to one.

issues.what: The Spotlight handler assigns `containerService.activeContainerId` directly instead of calling `setActive(_:)`, so the library switch skips both the existence guard and the UserDefaults write that `setActive` performs (ContainerService.swift:46-55).
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Opening a document from Spotlight silently puts the app in a library it will forget: relaunch and you are back in the previous one, wondering where the document went. And because the existence check is skipped, a Spotlight entry for a since-deleted library sets an active id that matches nothing, so `filteredDocuments` (DocumentLibraryView.swift:89) returns empty and the tab looks like an empty library rather than a stale link.
issues.fix: Replace the assignment with `containerService.setActive(containerId)`.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical navigation outcome for every valid id — `setActive` assigns the same published property on line 49. It adds the `containers.contains` guard, the UserDefaults persistence and the selection haptic that every other switch site in the app already gets. The `else` fallback at line 109 already handles the no-container case, so a rejected invalid id degrades to exactly the behaviour that branch was written for.

issues.what: The library chip strip is a plain horizontal `ScrollView` with no `ScrollViewReader`, so the active chip is never scrolled into view when the active library changes from anywhere other than a tap on a visible chip.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: With more than a few libraries, a Spotlight jump (ContentView.swift:107), a workspace reload (ContentView.swift:391), or a switch made from Semantic Search leaves you looking at a document list with the selected chip parked off-screen. There is no on-screen answer to "which library am I in", so you scroll the strip hunting for the highlighted pill before you trust anything below it.
issues.fix: Wrap the `ScrollView` in a `ScrollViewReader`, tag each pill with `.id(container.id)` inside `pillList` (line 92), and add `.onAppear` plus `.onChange(of: containerService.activeContainerId)` handlers that call `proxy.scrollTo(containerService.activeContainerId, anchor: .center)` inside a short animation.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Purely additive. The pill list, disambiguated duplicate names (line 82), the count badges, the context-menu storage and delete actions with their deliberate nil-ness (lines 108-118), and the existing `withAnimation { setActive }` tap path are all unchanged. This adds an affordance where there is currently none.

issues.what: Tab selection and the composer draft are plain `@State` with no `@SceneStorage` anywhere in the app, so neither survives state restoration after the system unloads the scene.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The draft is the sharper half. You type out a long, carefully worded question, get pulled into another app, come back after the system has reclaimed the scene, and the composer is empty — the app persists your transcript on background (ContentView.swift:329-330) but not the sentence you had not sent yet, which is the one piece of text only you could have produced. The tab reset is milder but still jarring: the app always reopens on Chat regardless of where you were working.
issues.fix: Change `selectedTab` to `@SceneStorage`, backing it with a `String` raw value since `ContentView.Tab` (line 65) has no raw type today; add a raw-value conformance or map through a small helper. Separately change `inputText` in ChatComposerV2.swift:26 to `@SceneStorage("chatDraft")`, keeping the existing clear-on-send at line 247.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Both remain ordinary mutable state with identical read and write semantics — `@SceneStorage` only adds a persistence backing. The screenshot-mode initial-tab override (ContentView.swift:60-62) still works because it writes the same property before first render. The draft's `onChange` handler at ChatComposerV2.swift:160 and the send path that clears it at line 247 are unaffected.

verdict.reason:
The FINDINGS are almost entirely real and correctly located — I opened every cite. What fails the gate is the FIXES: four of them, as written, would put untrue content on screen or would not work at all.

VERIFIED AS CLAIMED (code shape + reachability):
- Issue 1. ChatScreen.swift:600 `.task(id: ragService.containerService.activeContainerId)`; the unconditional cancel block is 605-608 and the unconditional `resetStreamingState()/isProcessing=false/stage=.idle` is 611-615, both above the container guards. `stopGeneration()` at 1818 does preserve the partial (1830-1838); this path does not. The `.task` restart-on-reappear premise is standard SwiftUI and is corroborated in-repo by the `isAppeared` flag (declared 285, set true 882, false 889) which only exists because the author saw these callbacks fire on tab switches. `needsDeviceCheck` is correctly flagged.
- Issue 2. MessageListV2.swift:128 `.onAppear` → 130 `scrollToBottom(animated: false)`, ungated; `isPinnedToBottom` is maintained at 150-154 and honoured by all three `onChange` handlers but not by `onAppear`. Confirmed.
- Issue 3. Two `.task` at 205 and 208 both calling `refreshAnalysis()` (818); `analyze()` sets `isAnalyzing = true` at LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:359 without clearing `currentProfile`; gate at AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:123. `profileCache` (declared 304) is written at 381, removed at 332/341, and NEVER READ — the dead-cache claim is exactly right.
- Issue 4. CompactAtlasSceneView (2833) has `.task(id: activeContainerId)` at 2897 and `.task(id: projectionMethod)` at 2900, both firing on appear, both entering `loadAndProject()` (3028) whose first line is `isLoading = true` (3029). Unlike `analyze()`, there is no `analysisTask?.cancel()` here, so these two genuinely run concurrently rather than one superseding the other. `points/colors/annotations` are @State (2849-2851) and survive; no camera state is held in SwiftUI, so it does die with the representable teardown.
- Issue 5. `.task` at 180 → `loadAllData()` (214) → `isLoading = true` (215); gate at 492.
- Issue 6. Two independent instances confirmed — ChatScreen.swift:520 and DocumentLibraryView.swift:1327, both unconditional — each carrying `@State isMinimized`(299)/`isDismissed`(300).
- Issue 8. ContentView.swift:107 assigns `activeContainerId` directly; `setActive` (ContainerService.swift:46-55) adds the `containers.contains` guard, the UserDefaults write and the haptic. Confirmed.
- Issue 9. ContainerPicker.swift:46 is a bare horizontal `ScrollView`; the only `ScrollViewReader`s in the app are IngestionQueueOverlay:70, ThinkingStreamView:146, MessageListV2:72. Confirmed.
- Issue 10. `@State inputText` at ChatComposerV2.swift:26; zero `@SceneStorage` in the repo. Confirmed.
- Summary claims: no `.id()` on any container (only per-row, and it missed one more per-row at MessageListV2.swift:321 — claim still holds); only GlossaryViews.swift:179 uses `NavigationStack(path:)`.
- The out-of-dimension note is right: SourceChipsView.swift:126 is now the ONLY remaining `onLongPressGesture` in the app, on a `.buttonStyle(.plain)` Button inside the horizontal ScrollView at line 34.

WHY confirmed=false: see anyFunctionalityLost. Issue 7's fix rests on a false premise about SwiftUI, and issues 3/4/5's fixes would display stale data under a new label.
verdict.anyFunctionalityLost:
Four losses, all in the fixes rather than the findings.

1. ISSUE 7 — the fix does not preserve what it claims and cannot deliver its benefit as written. Its `functionalityPreserved` asserts "NavigationStack tracks NavigationLink(destination:) pushes in its bound path as well as value-based links". That is false. A `path` binding tracks value-based links resolved through `navigationDestination`; view-based `NavigationLink(destination:)` pushes are not represented in the path, so clearing the path does not pop them. This repo has 18 `NavigationLink`s, only 3 value-based, and `navigationDestination` appears only in GlossaryViews.swift:183 and GlossaryView.swift:64. The exact link the fix names as safe — DocumentLibraryView.swift:204 — is destination-based. So the fix either does nothing for the Spotlight/deep-link case it was written for, or it forces migrating 15 destination-based links to value+`navigationDestination`, which is precisely the operation that drops destinations. Reject as specified; re-scope to a per-tab migration with the destination inventory enumerated first.

2. ISSUES 3, 4 and 5 — the "keep the previous content visible" fixes will show the user something untrue on a real data change, because they gate on emptiness rather than on identity.
   - Issue 3: `invalidateCache(for:)` is only called on library REMOVAL (ContentView.swift:395), not on library SWITCH. So with the proposed gate `if engine.isAnalyzing, engine.currentProfile == nil`, switching from library A to library B renders A's insights, recommended views and library stats underneath B's `libraryHeader` until the rebuild lands. Gate must also require `engine.currentProfile?.containerId == containerService.activeContainerId` (the field exists — it is compared at LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:342).
   - Issue 4: `isLoading = true` only when `points.isEmpty` means changing the projection picker leaves the old projection's cloud on screen while the control reads the new method, and switching library shows the previous library's atlas. Gate on "key differs from the last completed load", not on emptiness.
   - Issue 5: the fix changes the shared gate at line 492, which also serves `loadStatistics()` (1534, `isLoading = true` at 1535) reached from the scope picker at line 188. With `if isLoading, stats == nil`, changing scope leaves the previous scope's `documentStats` rows under the new scope header. `stats` itself is whole-store and re-scoped at render, so the headline is fine; the document list is not.

3. ISSUE 1 — the fix leaves a diagnostic frozen and reading wrong. If streaming now survives the tab return, the 5 Hz clock does not: `.onDisappear` (588-591) cancels `processingClockConnection`, and the only restart is `.onChange(of: isProcessing)` (578-587), which cannot fire because `isProcessing` never changed. Everything driven by `nowTick` (969, 995, 1533, 1539, 1549) then displays a stale elapsed time for the rest of the answer. Requires a companion: restart the clock in `.onAppear` (864) when `isProcessing` is true. Also prefer the `lastCancelledContainerId` variant over "move the block inside `if !isSameChatContainer`", because the `#if DEBUG didSeedScreenshotDemo { return }` at 619 sits above that branch and would silently drop the cancel in screenshot mode.

Not lost, clean as written: issues 2, 6, 8, 9, 10. Issue 6's claim that the deep link improves is correct — the notification handler at 481 currently un-dismisses both copies.

- Issue 3: `.refreshable` is at 211, not 210. `invalidateCache()` (wholesale) is the function at 330; 331 is its `currentProfile = nil`.
- Issue 4: the five settings `onChange` handlers are 2904-2908, not "2903-2907".
- Issue 5: the watchdog `Task` is at 220 (comment 218-219), not "218"; `.refreshable` is at 199, not 196; the scope-change reload is at 188, not 187.

SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDINGS THEMSELVES:
- Issue 3 overstates the symptom. `analyze()` does not clear `currentProfile`, and the hero 3D atlas gate at line 117 sits OUTSIDE the `isAnalyzing` branch — so `InlineTipView`, `hero3DAtlasSection` and `libraryHeader` all stay on screen during re-analysis. What actually swaps to the spinner is insights, recommended views, the expanded view and library stats. "Replaces its entire populated body" and "collapses to a fraction of its height so your scroll position is clamped to the top" are both wrong; the hero is the tallest section on the page. The finding is still real, just smaller than described.
- Issue 3's duplicate-analysis claim is real but self-limiting: `analyze()` opens with `analysisTask?.cancel()` (356), so the second `.task` supersedes the first. Issue 4 has no such guard, so THAT duplicate genuinely runs twice concurrently — the two findings should not be described in the same terms.
- Issue 1 understates the defect in one respect worth recording: the cancel block at 605-608 does not call `ragService.cancelActiveGeneration(...)`, which `cancelInFlightQueryWork()` (3019-3026) does. So the return discards the visible answer while the underlying generation may keep running. The user loses the output and the device keeps paying for it.
- Issue 7's "re-tapping the active tab does nothing" is asserted, not established. SwiftUI's `TabView` is UIKit-backed and pop-to-root on tab re-selection may come through from `UITabBarController` regardless of a path binding. Mark that sub-claim `needsDeviceCheck` rather than stating it.
- Summary claim (b) has a counterexample: ValidationDashboardView.swift:15 builds a view model in `View.init` via `StateObject(wrappedValue:)`. It is the safe idiom and it is not a tab root, so the point about the five tab roots stands, but "no view model is built in a View.init" as written is not true of the app.
- Issue 2 has an unstated dependency: the fix is only an improvement if `ScrollView` content offset actually survives the tab switch. If it does not, removing the forced scroll strands the user at the top, which is worse than today. That is the one thing in this report that must be checked on device before the edit, not after.

findings.summary: Seven real findings, all read off source with line anchors. The dominant pattern is not slowness — it is that three of the five tabs throw away content they already have in order to show a spinner. Database blanks its whole overview to "Loading database statistics..." on every return to the tab even though `stats` is still in `@State`; Atlas collapses its insights, recommended views and library stats to "Analyzing your library..." on every return even though `currentProfile` is a live singleton and a `profileCache` exists that is written, invalidated, and never once read. Atlas additionally runs its most expensive operation (full embedding hydration for the container) twice per appearance because of a redundant `.task` sitting next to a `.task(id:)`. Database's first open races its own scope seeding against its own initial load, doing every query twice and re-raising the spinner after content appeared. In Chat, the suggested-prompt card has no loading state at all: because "no results yet" and "no results, ever" are the same empty array, the card prints the terminal fail-closed verdict "No grounded suggestions are ready yet" while it is still working, then contradicts itself when chips pop in — and for any library that genuinely yields nothing, that same load is re-fired on every single entry to the Chat tab, forever. The load it is waiting on is itself mostly waste: it pulls a sample of chunks (which forces the whole vector store off disk via `allChunks()` → `awaitLoad()`), and `generateQuestions` discards that sample whenever the on-disk question bank is non-empty, which is the normal case. Two smaller flow breaks: the transcript is yanked to the bottom on every return to Chat regardless of where you were reading, and the composer text field is hard-disabled for the entire generation, so you cannot draft your next question while an answer streams. Every fix below is deferral, caching, or state-machine repair. None deletes a screen, an action, a diagnostic or a piece of copy — the fail-closed suggestion message, the 10s watchdog, the send guard, the pull-to-refresh force path and the "open at the newest message" behaviour all survive intact. Not covered here (belongs to the throughput audit): the launch hang, publisher storms, main-actor blocking, list construction. One thing I looked for and did not find: no second instance of the manual-long-press-inside-a-horizontal-ScrollView pattern survives — `ContainerPicker.swift:216-219` is now `.contextMenu` with the reasoning written down, and the only other `onLongPressGesture` (`SourceChipsView.swift:126`) uses `minimumDuration: 0` purely as a press-highlight, which does not contend with a pan.

issues.what: `loadAllData()` sets `isLoading = true` unconditionally and is attached to a bare `.task`, so returning to the Database tab replaces the entire, already-populated overview with a full-screen "Loading database statistics..." spinner while it re-fetches figures that are still sitting in `@State`.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You leave the Database tab, come back three seconds later, and the screen you were just looking at is gone — replaced by a spinner. The data never left; the app just decided to hide it from you. The team already knows this load can hang, because there is a 10-second watchdog at line 220 guarding it, which means the blank period is sometimes very long.
issues.fix: Make the spinner conditional on there being nothing to show: `if isLoading && stats == nil`. Keep rendering the existing `stats` during a refresh and let the new values swap in when they land. Optionally add a small inline refresh indicator in `headerSection` so the update is still visible. For the very first open, warm `SQLiteFullTextService.getStatistics()` from the app-level `.task` in ContentView (ContentView.swift:161) so the tab's first paint has figures ready rather than a cold spinner.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every figure, section, watchdog and refresh path is untouched. `loadAllData()` still runs, still repopulates `stats`, `documentStats`, and all Phase 2 diagnostics, and the watchdog at line 220 still force-clears `isLoading`. issues.whyItFeelsBad: The tab flashes: spinner, content, spinner, content. And every later scope change (picking a different library from the picker at line 444) wipes all four metric cards to a spinner rather than updating the numbers in place, so comparing two libraries means watching the screen empty out between each one.
issues.fix: Two changes. (a) Seed the scope before the load can observe it — give `databaseScope` its value in the same `.onAppear` that already guards on `didSeedScope`, and make the `.onChange(of: databaseScope)` handler skip while `didSeedScope` has only just been set, or simply initialise the scope from `containerService.activeContainerId` and drop the seeding `onAppear` entirely. issues.functionalityPreserved: The scope still defaults to the active library, which is the documented intent in the comment at lines 32-34. Every query still runs and every value still refreshes; `getIndexInfo()` still populates `indexInfo`, just off the critical path exactly as `loadAllData` already does at line 246. issues.what: `AdaptiveVisualizationsView` carries a bare `.task { await refreshAnalysis() }` immediately above `.task(id: containerService.activeContainerId) { await refreshAnalysis() }`. issues.whyItFeelsBad: Opening Atlas costs twice what it needs to, and the duplicate work happens at exactly the moment the user is staring at a spinner waiting for the tab to resolve.
issues.fix: Delete the bare `.task` at lines 205-207. `.task(id:)` at 208-210 fires on appearance and on every container change, which is a strict superset of what the bare one covered.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Nothing. `.task(id:)` runs on initial appearance and on id change; the bare `.task` runs only on initial appearance. Removing it cannot drop a trigger. Pull-to-refresh at line 211 is a separate modifier and is untouched.

issues.what: While a re-analysis runs, `engine.isAnalyzing` swaps the insights row, recommended-views grid, any expanded view and the library stats for a large "Analyzing your library..." card — even though `engine.currentProfile` is still populated (the engine is `LibraryVisualizationEngine.shared`, so it survives tab switches). Worse, `LibraryVisualizationEngine` maintains a `profileCache` (LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:304) that is written at line 381 and invalidated at 332/341 but is never read anywhere in the codebase, so `analyze()` recomputes from scratch every time.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Return to Atlas and the screen tears in half: the 3D scene is still there, fully rendered from a profile the app clearly still has, while everything beneath it has been replaced by a spinner claiming the library needs analysing. The same repo does this correctly elsewhere — `ProjectionCache` (Embedding3DView.swift:3202-3231) checks its cache before recomputing — so the write-only `profileCache` reads as an oversight rather than a decision.
issues.fix: Two parts. (a) In the view, change the branch to `if engine.isAnalyzing && engine.currentProfile == nil` so a refresh keeps the last profile on screen; move the analysing signal to a small inline indicator near `libraryHeader`. (b) In `LibraryVisualizationEngine.analyze`, actually read `profileCache`: add a cheap fingerprint (containerId plus documents.count, chunks.count, retrievalHistory.count) to the cached entry and return early — publishing the cached profile, insights and recommended views without setting `isAnalyzing` — when the fingerprint matches. Add a `force: Bool = false` parameter so `.refreshable` (line 211) can bypass the cache.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The analysing card still shows on a true cold analysis, when `currentProfile` is nil. Every insight, recommended view, expanded view and stat is computed by the same code path and is byte-identical; the cache only skips recomputing a result that the existing invalidation hooks (`invalidateCache(for:)`, already wired from ContentView.swift:395) already guarantee is stale-free. issues.what: The starter-prompt card has no loading state. `refreshSuggestedQuestions` only sets `isRefreshingSuggestions = true` inside `if force` (line 1648), so the non-forced path used on library switch and on tab entry never signals that it is working. With `dynamicSuggestedQuestions` cleared to `[]` at line 643, `starterPrompts` returns `[]` (line 1587), and `FirstQueryPromptView.supportingText` therefore prints its terminal fail-closed verdict — "No grounded suggestions are ready yet" (line 3744) — while the load is still in flight. Because an in-progress load and a genuinely empty result are the same empty array, `onAppear` (line 883) and `.task(id:)` (line 654) both re-fire the whole load on every single entry to the Chat tab for any library that legitimately yields no questions.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You tap a library chip and the app immediately tells you there is nothing to suggest — a settled, confident-sounding verdict — and then a second later contradicts itself by filling the card with chips. That is the opposite of the honesty this UI is built for: it states a conclusion it has not reached. And on a library that really does yield nothing, the app silently redoes the entire lookup every time you touch the Chat tab and prints the identical sentence.
issues.fix: Introduce a tri-state (`notLoaded` / `loading` / `loaded(questions)`) for the suggestions, replacing the `dynamicSuggestedQuestions.isEmpty` proxy. Set `loading` at the top of `refreshSuggestedQuestions` regardless of `force` (or add a separate `isLoadingSuggestions` flag alongside the existing `isRefreshingSuggestions`, which drives the spin animation on the refresh button). Give `supportingText` a loading branch that describes the action rather than promising an outcome — "Looking for grounded suggestions in this library…" — and show 3-4 dimmed skeleton rows in place of the prompt list. Keep the existing sentence at line 3744 for the `loaded` state with zero results. Gate the re-fire at lines 654 and 883 on the state being `notLoaded`, not on the array being empty.
issues.functionalityPreserved: The fail-closed message at line 3744 is kept verbatim and still shows whenever the load actually resolves with no grounded questions — that behaviour is the point of the design (see the header comment in SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:32) and is untouched. The manual refresh button, its spin animation, and the `force: true` path all keep working identically. The skeleton rows carry no text and imply no specific content, so they cannot suggest data that may not arrive; the loading sentence describes what the app is doing, not what it will find. Gating the retry on `notLoaded` does not remove a refresh route: document changes still invalidate through `.onReceive(ragService.$documents)` at line 661 and the user can still force a regeneration from the refresh button.

issues.what: Before the suggestion chips can appear, `refreshSuggestedQuestions` awaits `ragService.getSampleChunks(for:limit:)` for up to 160 chunks. That call goes to `db.allChunks()` (RAGService.swift:3928), which in `BNNSVectorDatabase` begins with `await awaitLoad()` (BNNSVectorDatabase.swift:680) — pulling the container's entire vector store off disk. `generateQuestions` then uses `sampleChunks` only when the on-disk question bank is empty (SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:488), and the bank is normally non-empty, so the whole fetch is discarded. The eager `await suggestedQuestionsService.invalidateCache(for: activeId)` at line 650 — invalidating the cache for the library being switched *to* — guarantees `hasValidCache` returns false and the fetch is always paid.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Tapping a library chip should be instant — `ContainerService.setActive` is just a UUID assignment and a UserDefaults write. Instead the chip highlights, the prompt card goes blank, and you wait on a full vector-store load for a value that is then thrown away. The cost scales with library size, so the bigger your library the worse switching into it feels, for no reason connected to what is being displayed.
issues.fix: Stop materialising the sample eagerly. Change `generateQuestions` to take a lazy provider — `sampleChunks: @Sendable () async throws -> [DocumentChunk]` — and invoke it only inside the `if bank.isEmpty` branch at SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:488. The caller then passes `{ try await ragService.getSampleChunks(for: containerId, limit: sampleLimit) }` and pays nothing on the common path. Separately, drop the eager `invalidateCache(for: activeId)` at line 650: it targets the library being switched to, so it only destroys the fast path. The cache is already invalidated on real content change via `.onReceive(ragService.$documents)` at line 670 and by `removeQuestions`/`clearQuestionBank` in the service.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical questions are produced. When the bank is empty the provider is called and `generateInitialBank` runs exactly as today, with the same limit computed the same way at line 1685. When the bank is non-empty the fetched value was already being discarded, so skipping it cannot change any output. Removing the eager invalidation does not stale the chips: the document-change hook at line 670 and the `documentCount` check inside `hasValidCache` (SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:591) both still force regeneration when the library's contents actually change, and the manual refresh button still forces unconditionally.

issues.what: `MessageListV2` calls `scrollToBottom(proxy:animated:false)` from an unconditional `.onAppear`, ignoring the `isPinnedToBottom` state it maintains at line 173 for exactly this purpose.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You scroll up to re-read an earlier answer, hop to Documents to check a source, come back — and you are dumped at the bottom of the transcript with no way back to where you were except scrolling again. The app forgets what you were reading every time you glance at another tab.
issues.fix: Gate the call: `if isPinnedToBottom { scrollToBottom(proxy: proxy, animated: false) }`. `isPinnedToBottom` is `@State`, initialised `true`, and is maintained by the preference-key handler at line 150, so a first appearance and any return-while-already-at-the-bottom still land at the newest message. If a device check shows SwiftUI is not preserving the scroll offset across tab switches on its own, keep a `@State lastVisibleMessageID` fed by the same preference machinery and `proxy.scrollTo` that id instead — restoring the position rather than abandoning it.
issues.functionalityPreserved: "Open the chat at the newest message" is kept: `isPinnedToBottom` starts `true`, so the first appearance behaves exactly as today, as does every return where the user had not scrolled away. Auto-follow during streaming (lines 132-149) is a different code path and is untouched; it already correctly guards on `isPinnedToBottom`. Nothing is removed — the only behaviour that changes is the one case that currently discards user state.

issues.what: The composer's `TextField` is `.disabled(isProcessing)`, so for the entire duration of a generation — which in Deep Think and Maximum modes is many seconds — the user cannot type, and the keyboard is dismissed because a disabled field resigns first responder. The attachment button also vanishes entirely at line 93.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The moment you send a question the app takes the keyboard away from you. Any follow-up you had half-formed has to wait, and when the answer finishes you have to tap back into the field and start typing from scratch. Every other chat interface lets you draft while the reply streams.
issues.fix: Remove `.disabled(isProcessing)` from the TextField and add `guard canSend else { return }` at the top of `send()` (line 218), which reinstates the exact block the `.disabled` was providing — `canSend` already requires `!isProcessing` at line 47. Keep the attachment button mounted but disabled rather than removing it at line 93, so the composer does not resize mid-generation. The send button already becomes Stop during processing (lines 128-148) and needs no change.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Sending during generation stays blocked, and now by an explicit guard rather than a side effect of a view modifier — which also closes a real gap, since `ChatScreen.sendMessage` (ChatScreen.swift:2471) has no `isProcessing` check of its own while `sendMessageWithAttachments` does (line 2318), so the `.disabled` was the only thing stopping the `onSubmit(send)` path at line 157. Stop, attachment picking, and every other composer affordance are unchanged; the attachment button becomes disabled rather than absent, so nothing is lost and the layout stops jumping.

verdict.reason:
All eight findings survive refutation on code shape and reachability; every line anchor resolves, with four minor citation slips noted below. But fix 4(b) fails the functionality gate on a verified-false premise.

CONFIRMED FINDINGS
1. DatabaseDashboardView.swift:214-215 `loadAllData()` sets `isLoading = true` unconditionally; bare `.task` at 180-183; watchdog at 220-226; spinner at 492-493. Confirmed.
2. Race confirmed: `.task` 180, `.onAppear` seeding 191-195, `.onChange(of: databaseScope)` 188-190, `loadStatistics` 1534-1540 with `getIndexInfo()` at 1538 in the blocking path versus its Phase 2 deferral at 251. Scope picker at 444. Confirmed.
3. AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:205-207 bare `.task` sits directly above `.task(id:)` at 208-210. Confirmed. Refinement, not a refutation: `analyze()` self-cancels at LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:355, so only one analysis completes — but both `refreshAnalysis()` calls independently `await ragService.allChunksForActiveContainer()` (line 828) before reaching `analyze`, so the embedding hydration genuinely doubles. The finding says this correctly.
4. Line 117 hero renders from `engine.currentProfile`; line 123 hides everything below on `engine.isAnalyzing`. `engine` is the shared singleton (line 18), so the profile survives tab switches and the torn-screen symptom is real. `profileCache` is write-only exactly as claimed.
5. ChatScreen.swift:1647-1649 force-only flag, 643 clears the array, 1587 returns `[]`, 3743-3744 prints the terminal verdict. Confirmed, with two narrowing conditions the finding does not state: `starterPrompts` returns curated prompts first for the sample workspace (1568) and onboarding prompts when `activeDocCount == 0` (1578), and the card only renders when `messages.isEmpty` (1562, 2052). The bad state is real-user-library-with-documents on an empty chat. Still real.
6. Confirmed end to end. `getSampleChunks` → `db.allChunks()` → `await awaitLoad()` at BNNSVectorDatabase.swift:680. `bank.isEmpty && !sampleChunks.isEmpty` gate at SuggestedQuestionsService.swift:488. Critically, `invalidateCache(for:)` at 578-581 clears only the in-memory `cachedQuestions`, never the on-disk bank — so the bank is normally non-empty and the sample is genuinely discarded, as claimed.
7. MessageListV2.swift:128-131 unconditional, `isPinnedToBottom` at 173, preference handler 150-155, streaming paths 132-148 correctly guarded. Confirmed.
8. ChatComposerV2.swift:87 `.disabled(isProcessing)`, 93 attachment button unmounted, `canSend` 44-48, `send()` 218 with no guard, `.onSubmit(send)` 157. Confirmed.

CITATION ERRORS (minor, none change a conclusion)
- `db.allChunks()` in `getSampleChunks` is RAGService.swift:3927, not 3928.
- The Chat `.task(id:)` is declared at ChatScreen.swift:600; line 654 is the `isEmpty` guard inside it.
- The Database spinner is scoped to `overviewSection` (line 492), not full-screen — the header, section picker and the other seven sections keep rendering, and `documentStats` is never cleared so the Documents section does not blank. Overview is the default section, so the practical complaint stands.
- Finding 8 characterises `.disabled` as "the only thing stopping the onSubmit path". `sendMessage` at ChatScreen.swift:2471 is not unguarded-and-dangerous: at 2489-2496 it explicitly cancels an in-flight query and proceeds. The behaviour being protected is "block", not "prevent corruption". The proposed guard still preserves it.

WHY 4(b) FAILS
The fix asserts "the existing invalidation hooks (`invalidateCache(for:)`, already wired from ContentView.swift:395) already guarantee is stale-free". That is false. All three call sites of `LibraryVisualizationEngine.invalidateCache(for:)` are container-DELETION paths: ContentView.swift:395, DocumentLibraryView.swift:1640, LibraryDeletion.swift:108. Document ingest (RAGService.swift:6040), document removal (6968) and `clearAllDocuments` (6993) invalidate `ProjectionCache` only and never touch the visualization profile cache. The no-argument `invalidateCache()` at line 330 has zero call sites anywhere. Today that gap is harmless because the cache is never read; making it read converts the missing hooks into live staleness.

CONDITIONS ON THE FIXES THAT DO PASS
- Fix 1: the inline refresh indicator must be mandatory, not "optional". Unlabelled stale figures on a diagnostics screen present a stale number as current, which is the failure `.claude/rules/user-facing-copy.md` names by hand.
- Fix 7: the gating-only variant must not ship unverified. If SwiftUI does not preserve the ScrollView offset across tab switches, gating the call lands the user at the TOP of a long transcript, which is worse than today. The finding names the `lastVisibleMessageID` fallback; the device check must decide which variant ships.
- Fix 6: dropping the eager invalidation at ChatScreen.swift:650 is safe on the paths I checked — `removeQuestions` invalidates at 254, `clearQuestionBank` at 261, `cacheMaxAge` is 300s at line 118, and `hasValidCache` checks `documentCount` at 591. One residual: the in-memory entry is returned at 476-482 BEFORE the deleted-document filter at 493-497, so a cached entry is never doc-filtered. The 5-minute TTL plus the count check bound it. Acceptable.
- Fix 8: keeping the field enabled means the keyboard can sit over the streaming answer. Not a loss — `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` is already at MessageListV2.swift:127 — but it is a visible change.
- Fix 3 is the only unconditionally clean one.
verdict.anyFunctionalityLost:
Fix 4(b) only. Two things go, both verified in source:

(1) The Atlas's guarantee that its profile reflects the current index. Today `refreshAnalysis()` recomputes on every appearance, so the Atlas self-corrects from any content change. A cache keyed on (containerId, documents.count, chunks.count, retrievalHistory.count) misses that correction for any change that preserves counts, and — since ingest/remove/clear never call `LibraryVisualizationEngine.invalidateCache` (they only invalidate `ProjectionCache`, RAGService.swift:6040, 6968, 6993) — nothing else catches it either. The Atlas would sit on a profile built from superseded data with no user-visible signal and no route back except pull-to-refresh. This is not hypothetical for the v5 embedding arc, whose additive-then-swap migration holds chunk count constant by design; that is precisely the fingerprint's blind spot.

(2) A live library-age and recent-additions readout. `LibraryProfile` embeds time-derived fields computed at build time (`libraryAge` from `Date().timeIntervalSince(oldestDoc.addedAt)`, LibraryVisualizationEngine.swift:423; `recentAdditions` at 415). Both are rendered — `formatAge(libraryAge)` at AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:1449 and `LibraryTimelineView(additions:libraryAge:)` at 751. A count-keyed cache with no TTL freezes them, so the Atlas prints a library age that stops advancing. That is the app stating a figure that is no longer true, on a screen whose whole job is describing the library.

Fix 4(a) — keeping the last profile on screen while re-analysing — loses nothing and should be kept; the hero section at line 117 already does exactly that. The rejection is 4(b) as specified. It becomes acceptable only if the cached entry carries a TTL and time-derived fields are recomputed on a hit, AND the missing invalidation hooks are added at RAGService.swift:6040/6968/6993 so a content change invalidates the profile the same way it already invalidates `ProjectionCache`. Both of those are additions to the fix, not readings of it.
verdict.correction:
Fix 4(b) must not ship as written. Replace it with: (i) add `LibraryVisualizationEngine.shared.invalidateCache(for:)` alongside the three existing `ProjectionCache.shared.invalidate(forContainer:)` calls at RAGService.swift:6040 (ingest), 6968 (document removal) and 6993 (clearAllDocuments), so content changes invalidate the profile the way they already invalidate the projection; (ii) give the cached entry a timestamp and a TTL, and recompute `libraryAge`/`recentAdditions` on a cache hit rather than serving the frozen values rendered at AdaptiveVisualizationsView.swift:1449 and 751; (iii) only then read `profileCache` in `analyze()`, and keep the `force: Bool = false` bypass for `.refreshable`. Fix 4(a) is clean as written and can proceed independently.

Also correct these anchors before the fixes are written up: `db.allChunks()` in `getSampleChunks` is RAGService.swift:3927 not 3928; the Chat `.task(id:)` is at ChatScreen.swift:600 (654 is the guard inside it); the Database spinner is `overviewSection`-scoped at line 492, not full-screen. And soften the finding-8 rationale — `sendMessage` at ChatScreen.swift:2471 already handles an in-flight query by cancelling it at 2489-2496, so the `.disabled` was blocking an interrupt-and-resend, not preventing state corruption. The proposed `guard canSend` still preserves current behaviour, so the fix stands; only the justification needs restating.

Two fixes need a device check gating them, per the finding's own needsDeviceCheck flag: fix 7 must not ship in its gating-only form until scroll-offset preservation across tab switches is confirmed on hardware, and fix 2's flash symptom depends on `.onAppear`/`.task` ordering that source reading cannot settle.

findings.summary: Real findings, and the pattern is consistent: the motion is *written* but not *wired*. Four separate transitions (message insertion, metrics bar, follow-up chips, writing-tools overlay) are declared in source and never run, because the state that drives them is mutated outside any animation transaction, or because `.animation(_:value:)` sits inside the `if` it is supposed to animate. MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-179 does it correctly, which is how you can tell the others are oversights rather than choices. The net effect is that the app's highest-intent moment — pressing Send — produces zero connecting motion: the bubble pops in, then an unrelated spring scrolls the list, and a metrics bar materialises above and shoves the conversation down in a hard jump. Second cluster: the streaming path animates what it says it does not (`scrollToBottom(animated: false)` runs `withAnimation`, MessageListV2.swift:167) on an arbitrary modulo throttle whose cadence depends on adaptive chunk size, producing jerky follow and yanking the user back when they read a few lines up. Third: the Silicon HUD defaults ON (SettingsStore.swift:581), is mounted on four of five tabs, and its blurred glow gets a fresh implicit animation 25 times a second from a MainActor pulse loop, over the list you are scrolling, during generation. Honest negative on one thing I was asked to check: `glassEffect` is NOT the scroll cost. It appears on chips, three buttons and two containers (Theme.swift:321-368 and five call sites) and on no list row; bubble shadows are opacity 0.04 / radius 2. The offscreen work worth measuring is the HUD's `.blur(radius:)` at MotherboardHUDView.swift:577 and 640, not the glass. Also: 14 `repeatForever` animations and exactly one reader of `accessibilityReduceMotion` (OnboardingChecklistView.swift:36) — Reduce Motion is honoured in onboarding and nowhere else. No hard-boundary file is involved in any fix; ChatScreen mutates `[ChatMessage]` but ChatMessage.swift itself needs no change.

issues.what: The message-insertion transition is declared but never runs: no site that mutates `messages` wraps the change in an animation transaction, so SwiftUI has no transaction to drive the insertion/removal.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: You press Send and the bubble is just suddenly there — no motion links your tap to the thing that appeared. A beat later the list springs to the bottom in a separate, unrelated animation, so the arrival reads as two disconnected events instead of one gesture landing.
issues.fix: Wrap the mutation sites in the same curve the scroll already uses: `withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8))` around `messages.append(userMessage)` (ChatScreen.swift:2516), `messages.append(message)` in appendAndPersistMessage (ChatScreen.swift:1729), and the two `messages.removeAll()` calls (ChatScreen.swift:1751, 1796). That puts the insertion and the existing `scrollToBottom(animated: true)` spring (MessageListV2.swift:162) in one transaction, so the bubble rises into place as the list follows it. Leave the `.transition` at MessageListV2.swift:92-95 exactly as written.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Nothing is removed or gated. The asymmetric transition already exists in source at lines 92-95 and is currently dead; this only supplies the transaction it needs. Message content, ordering, `persistChatHistory` and the container-override path are untouched — the change is purely the transaction wrapper around an assignment that already happens.

issues.what: `scrollToBottom(animated: false)` is animated — it runs `withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12))` — and it is driven by a modulo predicate whose firing rate depends on the adaptive streaming chunk size, not on time.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The transcript tracks the stream unevenly: glued for a stretch, then drifting, then snapping. And an animated programmatic scroll competes with your finger, so trying to re-read a few lines while an answer streams pulls you back down — you have to scroll more than the 80pt un-pin threshold (line 153-154) before the app will leave you alone.
issues.fix: In the `animated: false` branch (lines 166-169) call `proxy.scrollTo("bottom", anchor: .bottom)` with no `withAnimation`, so the follow is a plain offset set that a touch can override. Replace the `newText.count % 80 < 20` predicate at line 140 with a time-based throttle (store a `lastAutoScroll: Date` and scroll at most every ~100ms), so cadence no longer swings with the 50/80/120-char adaptive chunk sizes chosen at ChatScreen.swift:3053-3071.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Auto-follow during streaming stays, the pin/un-pin detection via BottomAnchorYPreferenceKey stays, the 80pt threshold stays, and the `animated: true` spring path for new messages and thinking events (lines 134, 148) is untouched. Only the streaming branch stops animating and starts throttling on a clock instead of on character count.

issues.what: `withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.04))` wraps a plain string append in the streaming pump, opening an animation transaction over the whole transcript subtree 12-25 times a second for a mutation that cannot interpolate.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: Arriving text looks soft and smeary rather than crisp, and these transactions overlap the animated scroll from the same state change, so two competing animations run on the same view every pump tick — at the exact moment the device is busiest generating.
issues.fix: Append plainly: `streamingText.append(nextChunk)` with no `withAnimation`. If the soft reveal was intentional, express it locally instead — `.contentTransition(.opacity)` on the streaming `MarkdownText` (MessageListV2.swift:232-236) animates the glyph swap without opening a transaction that reaches the rest of the list.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Identical characters at an identical cadence. The adaptive backlog logic (chunk size 50/80/120, cadence 40/60/80ms, lines 3057-3071), the `updateSpeedHistory()` sparkline call at line 3083, and the finish-fast path all stay exactly as they are. Only the scope of the animation transaction changes.

issues.what: Three transitions are placed inside the `if` branch they are meant to animate, with `.animation(_:value:)` also inside the branch, so the modifier is torn down along with the content and neither insertion nor removal animates. None of the driving state is mutated inside `withAnimation`.
issues.whyItFeelsBad: The instant you send, a metrics bar materialises above the transcript and shoves the entire conversation down in one frame, while the follow-up chip row vanishes in the same frame. Two hard layout jumps stacked on the app's most-repeated action. It reads as the screen glitching rather than responding.
issues.fix: Hang the animation off a parent that survives the swap: put `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: consolidatedMetricsData != nil)`, `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25), value: followUpSuggestions.isEmpty)` and `.animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8), value: writingToolsProcessing)` on the `mainContentArea` VStack (line 2012) and delete the in-branch copies at 2027, 2141 and 2166. Alternatively wrap the mutations (2116, 2250, 2280, 2285, 2484, 2831, 636, 1766, 1809, 1880) in `withAnimation`. MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-179 with its transition at line 209 is the working template already in this codebase.
issues.functionalityPreserved: Every bar appears and disappears at exactly the same times, on the same conditions, with the same content. The `.transition` declarations stay where they are. Nothing is hidden, delayed past its trigger, or removed — the only change is that three already-written transitions start running.

New Chat and Clear Chat (lines 1751, 1796) cut back just as abruptly. Because the gate is `messages.isEmpty` (line 1562), the list view identity dies on every flip, so `isPinnedToBottom` (MessageListV2.swift:173) resets too.

issues.whyItFeelsBad: There is a blurred glow re-animating 25-33 times a second on top of the list you are trying to scroll, and it runs hardest during generation — precisely when the main thread has least headroom. Separately, a user who turns on Reduce Motion still gets shimmer bars, a blinking cursor, spinning icons and pulsing pills, because 14 `repeatForever` sites exist and only OnboardingChecklistView.swift:36 reads the setting.
issues.fix: Drive the sine oscillation from a single `repeatForever` animation (or a TimelineView) on one value, instead of 25 discrete state writes per second that each restart the `.animation(.linear(duration: 0.03), value: intensity)` at MotherboardHUDView.swift:615 (also 663, 702) over the `.blur(radius:)` at 577 and 640. Separately, read `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` at the `repeatForever` sites — MessageListV2.swift:254 and 370, RetrievalSourcesTray.swift:189, StatusPillV2.swift:106, UnifiedMetricsBar.swift:520, 1174, 1262, ThinkingStreamView.swift:355, ModelStatusIndicator.swift:124, LiveTelemetryStatsView.swift:115, Theme.swift:223 — and substitute a static value when it is on.

The oscillation looks the same; it is produced by one animation instead of 25 restarts per second. Honouring Reduce Motion adds respect for a setting the user chose — it removes no animation from anyone who has not asked for that.

issues.what: The suggestion-refresh icon rewinds when it finishes: `rotationEffect(.degrees(isRefreshing ? 360 : 0))` targets 0° on completion and the `.default` branch eases it backwards from wherever the loop stopped.

verdict.reason:
EVERY LINE CITATION IS ACCURATE. I opened all 40-odd cited sites and none was misquoted or misnumbered. Confirmed verbatim: MessageListV2.swift:92-95 (dead asymmetric transition), :140 (`newText.count % 80 < 20`), :160-171 (the `animated: false` branch really does call `withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12))`), :150-155 (80pt threshold via BottomAnchorYPreferenceKey, plumbing at :438-455 is real); ChatScreen.swift:1729/1751/1796/2516 (four unwrapped `messages` mutations), :2026-2027, :2140-2141, :2165-2166 (three `.transition` + `.animation(_:value:)` pairs inside the `if` they gate), :2052 + :1562 (`shouldShowFirstQueryHero` == `messages.isEmpty`, hard swap), :3078 (`withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.04))` around a string append), :3053-3071 (adaptive 50/80/120 chunk, 40/60/80ms cadence), :3817-3823 (rotation targets 0 on completion with `.default`); all ten "alternative" mutation lines (636, 1766, 1809, 1880, 2116, 2250, 2280, 2285, 2484, 2831) are exactly what the finding says they are; HardwareTelemetryState.swift:461-481 (25Hz MainActor loop, reachable from :438), MotherboardHUDView.swift:577/640 blur, :615/663/702 `.animation(.linear, value: intensity)`; SettingsStore.swift:581 defaults `showSiliconHUD = true` (path is Services/Infrastructure/Configuration/, not UI/Settings/); HUD mounted at ChatScreen:533, DocumentLibraryView:1366, DatabaseDashboardView:170, SettingsView:70 — four of five tabs, confirmed; exactly 14 `repeatForever` and exactly one `accessibilityReduceMotion` reader (OnboardingChecklistView.swift:36, used at :477 and :1021); MessageBubbleV2.swift:175-179 + :209 is a genuine working template; ContainerPicker.swift:216-229 documents the exact gesture migration cited.

ONE FINDING IS REFUTED ON REACHABILITY (issue 6). `SourceChipsView` has exactly two non-preview call sites: RetrievalSourcesTray.swift:112 and ChatScreen.swift:791. `RetrievalSourcesTray` has ZERO references anywhere in the repo outside its own file and its `#Preview` — it is dead UI. ChatScreen.swift:791 is inside `.sheet(isPresented: $showRetrievedDetails)`, in the `else` branch taken only when `currentMetadata == nil`. So source chips never appear in the transcript, are never inside a LazyVStack row, and the stated symptom — "scrolling back up through the transcript makes old answers' source chips flutter in again" — cannot occur. The code shapes at :38-43, :58-63 and :126-130 are exactly as described, but they sit on a rare sheet path. The finding also equates :126 with the already-fixed ContainerPicker case; it is not the same shape — that one was `minimumDuration: 0.45` plus a `confirmationDialog`, this is `minimumDuration: 0` with `perform: {}`, a press-state tracker. The stuck-pressed-state risk is plausible; the swallowed-scroll risk is not supported.

TWO SYMPTOM CLAIMS ARE OVERSTATED. (a) Issue 3's "text looks soft and smeary": `streamingText` is a plain `String` into `MarkdownText`; glyphs are not interpolatable, so the 0.04s transaction can only animate the bubble's height growth over 40ms — imperceptible. The defensible harm is transaction scope (an ambient animation over every view that changes in that update, 12-25x/sec), not smeariness. The proposed alternative `.contentTransition(.opacity)` is also unsound: `contentTransition` is inert without an animated transaction, and the same fix removes the only one. (b) Issue 5's "discards scroll position and pinned-to-bottom state": true mechanically, but the swap only fires on `messages.isEmpty` flipping, i.e. first send (nothing to preserve), New Chat and Clear Chat (intentional reset), and thread load at :549 (fresh content). No user-reachable case actually loses a scroll position. The hard-cut symptom itself is real; the state-loss framing is not. Issue 5's side note is correct and important: `EmptyStateV2` (MessageListV2.swift:75-78) IS unreachable, because MessageListV2 is instantiated only at ChatScreen:2074, inside the `!messages.isEmpty` branch.

ONE FINDING IS STRONGER THAN STATED. Issue 2 undersells itself. When backlog > 400 the adaptive chunk is exactly `max(80, 50)` = 80 (ChatScreen.swift:3061-3063), so `streamingText.count` increments by exactly 80 and `count % 80` is a CONSTANT residue for the whole burst. If that residue is >= 20, `shouldScroll` is false on every tick and auto-follow stops entirely for the duration of the fast burst — not merely uneven, silently absent. This is the repo's own silent-truncation shape in a UI predicate. Separately, `BottomAnchorGeometry` republishes on every content-growth frame, so `isPinnedToBottom` can transiently compute false mid-stream before the scroll catches up — supporting the "glued, then drifting" description. Both are needsDeviceCheck for the visible result, but the modulo lockout is provable from source.

WHY confirmed IS false: the hard gate is functionality, and two fixes as written delete behaviour that currently works (named in anyFunctionalityLost). Everything else in the report survives.
verdict.anyFunctionalityLost:
Three things, all in the fixes rather than the findings.

(1) THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Issue 4's fix says "delete the in-branch copies at 2027, 2141 and 2166". Line 2141 and 2166 are genuinely dead — their `value:` (`followUpSuggestions.isEmpty`, `writingToolsProcessing`) is invariant inside the branch that mounts them, so they can never fire, and deleting them costs nothing. Line 2027 is NOT dead. Its value is `metricsData.tokens`, not a presence predicate, and `tokens` changes continuously while the bar stays mounted during streaming — so that modifier currently animates the live token counter and works. The proposed parent-level replacement is keyed on `consolidatedMetricsData != nil` and does not cover token changes. Deleting 2027 removes a working animated readout on the metrics bar. Fix: keep ChatScreen.swift:2027 exactly as written, delete only 2141 and 2166, and ADD the presence-keyed animations on the `mainContentArea` VStack (which begins at line 2012, and the finding's "line 2012" is right). The finding's own framing — "`.animation(_:value:)` sits inside the `if` it is supposed to animate" — is true for two of the three and false for the metrics one.

(2) Issue 6's fix offers "drop the per-index `.delay(Double(index) * 0.05)` at line 39 so the row is simply present". That deletes the staggered reveal, which is a deliberate affordance (documented in the file header, SourceChipsView.swift:6 and :16). Since the replay symptom is refuted anyway — the chips only ever render inside a sheet, where a one-time stagger is exactly right — there is no reason to pay for it. Keep the stagger; take only the `ButtonStyle`/`configuration.isPressed` half of the fix, which preserves the press affordance and fixes the stuck-state risk with no loss.

(3) Issue 7's reduce-motion clause says "substitute a static value when it is on". At several of those sites the motion IS the signal: ShimmerBar (MessageListV2.swift:370, RetrievalSourcesTray.swift:189) means "searching", the blinking cursor (MessageListV2.swift:254) means "streaming", StatusPillV2.swift:106 and ThinkingStreamView.swift:355 mean "active". A static value that resolves to the invisible end of the oscillation would remove the only in-progress cue for users who turned Reduce Motion on — an accessibility regression delivered under an accessibility fix. The requirement must be stated as: substitute a static VISIBLE state (cursor solid on, shimmer bar present at full opacity, pill at full tint), never the off-phase. With that constraint it loses nothing.

Not lost, contrary to what one might expect: issue 7's HUD change costs no diagnostic fidelity. `aneIntensity`/`gpuIntensity`/`cpuIntensity` are read only inside MotherboardHUDView (:331, :337-338, :352-353, :456-457, :601-608, :1016) and only for opacity, glow radius and a `> 0.01` active-component list. Nothing records or displays a number, and the 0.8-1.0 pulse multiplier never crosses the 0.01 gate, so collapsing 25 writes/sec into one view-side oscillation changes no reported value and breaks no `aneActiveTime` bookkeeping in `setIntensity` (HardwareTelemetryState.swift:689). Issues 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 lose nothing either — with one implementation requirement on issue 2: a time-based throttle must force a final scroll when `isStreaming` flips false, or the last sub-100ms chunk sits unscrolled. The existing `.onChange(of: messages.count)` at MessageListV2.swift:132 covers the normal finish (the assistant message is appended) and the stopGeneration partial-save path, so nothing is permanently lost, but the flush at ChatScreen.swift:3044-3050 deserves an explicit trailing scroll.

REVISED anyFunctionalityLost, one line: the tokens-keyed metrics animation at ChatScreen.swift:2027, and the source-chip stagger at SourceChipsView.swift:39-41.

Keep all eight findings, with these amendments.

ISSUE 6 — downgrade to a cleanup, and correct the symptom. Its stated symptom (transcript chips replaying on scroll) is impossible: `RetrievalSourcesTray` is dead code (zero call sites outside its own file and `#Preview`), and the only live `SourceChipsView` mount is ChatScreen.swift:791, inside the `showRetrievedDetails` sheet's `currentMetadata == nil` fallback. Take only the `ButtonStyle`/`configuration.isPressed` swap for SourceChipsView.swift:126-130; keep the stagger. Do not describe it as the ContainerPicker pattern — that was a 0.45s press plus a `confirmationDialog`, this is a 0-duration press tracker. Separately worth raising with the owner: RetrievalSourcesTray.swift is an entire unreferenced source-provenance component, which is a scope question, not an animation one.

ISSUE 4 — keep ChatScreen.swift:2027. Delete only 2141 and 2166. Add the presence-keyed `.animation(_:value:)` modifiers on the `mainContentArea` VStack at line 2012. Flag for device check that three `.animation(_:value:)` modifiers on that VStack apply to the WHOLE subtree, including `ChatComposerV2` and `MessageListV2`; because `followUpSuggestions = []` fires on every send (line 2484) at the same instant as issue 1's spring on `messages.append` (line 2516), two different curves will contend over the transcript in that frame.

ISSUE 3 — restate the harm as transaction scope, not smeariness. Drop the `.contentTransition(.opacity)` alternative; it is inert once the transaction is removed.

ISSUE 2 — strengthen. Say that at chunk size 80 the modulo residue is constant for the whole burst, so auto-follow can be absent rather than merely uneven. Add the requirement that the new time throttle fire a trailing scroll when `isStreaming` goes false.

ISSUE 1 — note the fix is partial. Four sites are cited; `messages` is also mutated unwrapped at ChatScreen.swift:939 (writing-tools insert-as-reply) and :1859/:1862 (regenerate removal, the only real removal path a user can trigger). Those keep the pop-in unless included. Also correct the mechanism claim: `withAnimation` around the append does not put the insertion and the scroll in ONE transaction — `scrollToBottom` opens its own at MessageListV2.swift:162. They are two transactions with matching curves starting in the same runloop turn, which is close enough in practice but should not be asserted as one.

ISSUE 5 — drop the scroll-position-loss claim; no user-reachable path loses one. Keep the hard-cut symptom and keep the `EmptyStateV2` unreachability note, which is confirmed.
